1.explanation: The root of the problem is the ‘namespace’ regex in components/prism-java.js. It’s defined as /(...\s+)[a-z]\w*(?:\.[a-z]\w*)+/, which requires at least one ‘.’ segment, so single-segment package names never match. Adjusting this pattern (for example by making the ‘(?:\.[a-z]\w*)+’ part optional with ‘*’ instead of ‘+’) will allow ‘package baz;’ to be recognized as a namespace and highlighted properly.
1.bug_scenario: In the Java code snippet, the syntax highlighter correctly highlights multi‐segment package names (e.g. “package baz.zap;”) as a namespace but fails to highlight single‐segment package names (e.g. “package baz;”). The provided screenshot shows “baz.zap” in yellow but “baz” left unhighlighted.

2.explanation: Both the unminified and minified Java language definitions register a "namespace" token with a regex that requires at least one dot in the name (the pattern uses (?:\.[a-z]\w*)+). This excludes single-segment package names. To fix the bug, the regex should allow zero or more dot-segments (e.g. change + to *), so that single-package names like “baz” are also matched and highlighted.
2.bug_scenario: The Java syntax highlighter fails to recognize and highlight single-segment package names. In the screenshot, “package baz;” does not highlight “baz” as a namespace token, while multi-segment names like “package baz.zap;” and imports such as “import foo.bar.Bar;” are highlighted correctly.
